{"additions":375,"autoMergeRequest":null,"baseRefName":"main","body":"Part 3 of #2190's [agreed split](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2190#issuecomment-5499945525), following the merged canonical resolver in #2241 and checkpoint migration in #2254.

Session construction, adoption, and sweep still use separate paths to resolve Git metadata. This PR moves the explicit-root consumers to `gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata`, so the canonical resolver supplies the common directory and worktree ID while each caller keeps its own storage and failure policy.

## Session-store construction

Previously, constructing a session store for a known worktree root ran `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, even though the root was already known.

`NewStateStoreForWorktree` now resolves `WorktreeMetadata.CommonDir` directly. Known-root construction therefore starts no Git subprocesses and checks the current metadata on every call. For example, if `commondir` is changed to point at a missing directory after a successful construction, the next construction fails. Repairing the metadata makes construction succeed again and preserves access to the saved session. Inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, and `GIT_WORK_TREE` values also cannot redirect an explicitly scoped store into another repository.

`NewStateStore`, the CWD constructor, intentionally stays on `gitdir.CommonDir`. The strategy's per-session state lock resolves through that same function, and the store and its lock must agree on one common directory. If the store moved to the canonical resolver alone, an exported `GIT_DIR` would place state files in the worktree's own `.git` while the lock went to the repository `GIT_DIR` names. Two writers of one state file would then hold different locks. Keeping both on one resolver also keeps split `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` setups working for session state. The CWD store moves to the canonical resolver together with the lock.

The common directory still feeds the existing rooted store. Linked worktrees share session files, and empty-root rejection, test isolation, no-follow I/O, atomic writes, and locking remain in place.

## Adoption and sweep

Adoption uses the canonical resolver for source and target worktree IDs. This removes its dependency on the legacy parser's expected directory names. A linked worktree backed by a bare repository named `storage`, for example, can now resolve its ID from `storage/worktrees/<id>`.

Hook paths still derive worktree IDs with `paths.GetWorktreeID`. Both resolvers yield the same ID for main and linked worktrees under `.git/` or `.bare/`. Only the canonical resolver also accepts a bare repository with any other name, and hooks cannot start sessions in that layout yet. Hook callers move to the canonical resolver with the strategy migration.

The source and target retain different failure policies. If source metadata cannot resolve, adoption can still match the session by its recorded worktree path. If target metadata cannot resolve, adoption stops before saving the adopted state. The combined Git query in `stateStoreForWorktree` stays because it validates an arbitrary user-supplied repository; a directory that merely contains an empty `.git` folder must still be rejected. Source-retirement rollback remains unchanged.

Sweep now resolves metadata from the worktree root it has already discovered. If that fails, it skips spawning. On success, it uses the common directory for the existing repository-wide throttle, so session starts in different worktrees continue to share the same throttle marker.

## Why the legacy APIs and cache remain

`session.GetGitCommonDir`, the cache-clearing API, and `gitdir`'s common-directory resolver and cache still serve the CWD session store, the session lock, strategy, and other consumers outside this slice. Removing them now would require migrating those callers too. Their deletion waits until those callers have migrated and been verified.

This PR changes three production files and their tests, plus a comment-only fix in `gitdir/gitdir.go` that drops a stale list of callers. The ownership guard remains active, and its ledger reasons now name the callers that still use the legacy resolvers. Rooted-handle lifetime and the strategy and session-lock migration stay with their existing owners.

## Verification

- `mise run lint`: passed with zero issues after merging main.
- `mise run test:integration`: passed.
- `mise run test`: passed except for two tests that timed out while a second copy of the suite was running on the same machine. They were `TestExtractPluginBinary_OversizeEntryIsRejected`, which hit the package's 10-minute limit, and `TestInstallHooks_ReclaimedChainRunsEachHookOnce/bash_template`, whose hook was killed. Both pass on their own with `-race`, and neither touches session state or locking.
- After merging main: session, gitrepo, strategy session-state, hook, and preview tests, plus adoption, sweep, and pending-checkpoint tests, pass. The pending-preview tests pass now that #2770 is in.

Focused tests cover linked-worktree save/load/clear, invalid roots, explicit-root metadata damage and repair, inherited Git variables on explicit roots, and adoption validation and source-path fallback. They also cover bare-backed worktree IDs and sweep failure/throttle behavior. `TestSessionStateAndLockHonorExportedGitDir` pins that the CWD store and its lock land in the same common directory when `GIT_DIR` points at another repository and in a split `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` layout. It failed against the earlier revision of this branch and passes now. Existing tests exercise rooted storage, symlink refusal, and adoption rollback.

Real Git Trace2 events show constructor subprocess counts:

| Construction path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CWD | 1 common-directory query | 1 common-directory query (unchanged) |
| Explicit root | 1 | 0 |

The Trace2 test includes a positive control that launches Git and checks that an additional event is recorded. These measurements cover store construction, not total hook latency.

Part 3 of #2190's [agreed split](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2190#issuecomment-5499945525), following the merged canonical resolver in #2241 and checkpoint migration in #2254.

Session construction and adoption still use separate paths to resolve Git metadata. This PR moves the explicit-root consumers to `gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata`, so the canonical resolver supplies the common directory and worktree ID while each caller keeps its own storage and failure policy.

## Session-store construction

Previously, constructing a session store for a known worktree root ran `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, even though the root was already known.

`NewStateStoreForWorktree` now resolves `WorktreeMetadata.CommonDir` directly. Known-root construction therefore starts no Git subprocesses and checks the current metadata on every call. For example, if `commondir` is changed to point at a missing directory after a successful construction, the next construction fails. Repairing the metadata makes construction succeed again and preserves access to the saved session. Inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, and `GIT_WORK_TREE` values also cannot redirect an explicitly scoped store into another repository.

`NewStateStore`, the CWD constructor, intentionally stays on `gitdir.CommonDir`. The strategy's per-session state lock resolves through that same function, and the store and its lock must agree on one common directory. If the store moved to the canonical resolver alone, an exported `GIT_DIR` would place state files in the worktree's own `.git` while the lock went to the repository `GIT_DIR` names. Two writers of one state file would then hold different locks. Keeping both on one resolver also keeps split `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` setups working for session state. The CWD store moves to the canonical resolver together with the lock.

The common directory still feeds the existing rooted store. Linked worktrees share session files, and empty-root rejection, test isolation, no-follow I/O, atomic writes, and locking remain in place.

## Adoption

Adoption uses the canonical resolver for source and target worktree IDs. This removes its dependency on the legacy parser's expected directory names. A linked worktree backed by a bare repository named `storage`, for example, can now resolve its ID from `storage/worktrees/<id>`.

Hook paths still derive worktree IDs with `paths.GetWorktreeID`. Both resolvers yield the same ID for main and linked worktrees under `.git/` or `.bare/`. Only the canonical resolver also accepts a bare repository with any other name, and hooks cannot start sessions in that layout yet. Hook callers move to the canonical resolver with the strategy migration.

The source and target retain different failure policies. If source metadata cannot resolve, adoption can still match the session by its recorded worktree path. If target metadata cannot resolve, adoption stops before saving the adopted state. The combined Git query in `stateStoreForWorktree` stays because it validates an arbitrary user-supplied repository; a directory that merely contains an empty `.git` folder must still be rejected. Source-retirement rollback remains unchanged.

## Why the legacy APIs and cache remain

`session.GetGitCommonDir`, the cache-clearing API, and `gitdir`'s common-directory resolver and cache still serve the CWD session store, the session lock, the session sweep, strategy, and other consumers outside this slice. Removing them now would require migrating those callers too. Their deletion waits until those callers have migrated and been verified.

The sweep stays on `session.GetGitCommonDir` on purpose. It finds stuck sessions through the CWD store, so its throttle marker has to come from the same resolver. Moving the sweep alone to the canonical resolver would break split `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` layouts: the work tree has no `.git`, so the sweep would find stuck sessions and then skip spawning on every session start. The sweep moves together with the CWD store.

This PR changes two production files and their tests, plus a comment-only fix in `gitdir/gitdir.go` that drops a stale list of callers. The ownership guard remains active, and its ledger reasons now name the callers that still use the legacy resolvers. Rooted-handle lifetime and the strategy and session-lock migration stay with their existing owners.

- `mise run check`: passed after keeping the sweep on its existing resolver, including formatting, zero-issue lint, unit and integration tests, and the deterministic Vogon and roger-roger canaries.

Focused tests cover linked-worktree save/load/clear, invalid roots, explicit-root metadata damage and repair, inherited Git variables on explicit roots, and adoption validation and source-path fallback. They also cover bare-backed worktree IDs. `TestSessionStateAndLockHonorExportedGitDir` pins that the CWD store and its lock land in the same common directory when `GIT_DIR` points at another repository and in a split `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` layout. It failed against the earlier revision of this branch and passes now. Existing tests exercise rooted storage, symlink refusal, and adoption rollback.

Real Git Trace2 events show constructor subprocess counts:

| Construction path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CWD | 1 common-directory query | 1 common-directory query (unchanged) |
| Explicit root | 1 | 0 |

The Trace2 test includes a positive control that launches Git and checks that an additional event is recorded. These measurements cover store construction, not total hook latency.
